_comment: Container image pinning policy. Every third-party image and Dockerfile base image is pinned to a DIGEST, not a tag — a tag is a moving target, so `:latest` means you cannot say what you are running until you look. Digests make the stack reproducible and make an upgrade a visible, reviewable diff. BUT: pinning WITHOUT an update process is worse than :latest, because you silently freeze on a vulnerable image. That is what reviewBy exists for — scripts/image_policy_check.py FAILS once the date passes, the same forcing-function pattern as context/model-policy.json. See ai-standards/references/dependency-security.md.
_reviewBy_note: Monthly, not quarterly: the orchestration tier in this stack has a heavy critical-CVE record (n8n shipped multiple CVSS 9.4-10.0 RCEs in 2026). Re-resolve digests, read the changelogs, re-run the scan, then move this date.

images.risk: HIGHEST in the stack. Executes user-supplied workflow expressions by design, so arbitrary code execution IS the product and the attack surface is structural. 2026 CVEs incl. CVE-2026-21858 (CVSS 10.0 unauth RCE), CVE-2026-25049 (9.4 unauth RCE), CVE-2026-27495/27497 (9.4). Mitigated here by binding to 127.0.0.1 only and holding no repo mount.
Host-exposed on 127.0.0.1:8090. Third-party, smaller project — least visibility into its security process of anything here. Treat as untrusted; it holds no secret and mounts nothing.
Low. stdlib only — no pip install, so no third-party dependency surface at all. Runs non-root with read-only mounts.

Router and scrubber are the privileged path — the router writes the audit ledger, the scrubber is the only holder of the PII vault. npm dependency surface is the supply-chain exposure here; see the lockfile rules in the lens.
Deliberately NOT firewalled (the research phase sniffs arbitrary APIs) and profile-gated off by default. Highest-privilege lane when running — start it explicitly and supervise it.

CI-only, never in the runtime stack. Pinned deliberately rather than using the marketplace trivy-action: a third-party GitHub Action runs arbitrary code with repo context inside a security-critical pipeline. Safe to pin — Trivy fetches its vulnerability DB at run time, so a pinned binary still sees fresh CVEs; only the scanner engine is frozen.

notPinned.why: Built locally from this repo. Their reproducibility comes from the pinned FROM digests above plus the committed source, so a tag is sufficient.

_pendingBumps_note: Version drift FOUND BY scripts/research_watch.py and deliberately deferred to the next review rather than bumped on the spot. Recorded so the deferral is a decision with a date, not a thing someone forgot. image_policy_check.py prints these on every run, so the queue cannot be missed while reading the policy it belongs to.

pendingBumps.why: Two minor versions behind on the highest-risk component in the stack. The watch attached NO security or deprecation signal to 2.31-2.32, so this is routine currency, not an incident — fold it into the scheduled re-pin. If a security signal lands on n8n before then, this stops being routine and the re-pin happens immediately.
pendingBumps.action: Re-resolve the digest, read 2.31/2.32 changelogs, re-run Trivy, move reviewBy.
